newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INTERVIEW-LATVIA'S TRASTA BANK EYES LITHUANIA.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-LATVIA'S TRASTA BANK EYES LITHUANIA.

text.p: The head of small but growing Latvian bank Trasta Bank said on Thursday his company was considering expanding its activities into Lithuania.

"We are looking at some targets in Lithuania...The future in banking in the region is in having a pan-Baltic presence," Trasta Bank chairman Girts Melbardis told Reuters at a Baltic investment conference in the Swedish capital.
He was not sure whether the bank would offer universal banking services outside Latvia or act as an investment fund.
Trasta was also looking at the possibility of taking over some smaller Latvian banks.
"If we did this we would probably tap the international capital markets," he added.
The bank, the 14th largest, currently has a capital adequacy ratio of 40 percent and is looking for 1.5 to two million lats of profit in 1997 with a return on equity of 50 percent.
"It is too early for us to seek a bourse listing," he added.
